title: Group-held-out tests do not separate age and corotation control of CPV rates in 763 TESS rotators
abstract: We test whether corotation radius ratio predicts complex periodic variable (CPV) labels better than period and age when each BANYAN best group is excluded from the fit. In 763 TESS rapid rotators with 75 CPVs in 25 groups, a bounded event model gives held-out log loss 222.642 for BHAC15 corotation ratio, 242.512 for period alone, and 223.384 for period plus age. The corotation gain over the age model is 0.742, with a fixed-score group-bootstrap range of -7.880 to 8.989. The gain changes sign in targets first observed after sector 55. Adding a photometric radius residual does not consistently improve prediction. These tests support an age-dependent signal beyond rotation, but do not select contraction as its cause. The radius computed from group age can encode a direct age effect. Shared labels, selected targets, uncertain ages, noisy radii and fixed efficiency calibration limit this reanalysis. No independent ages, spectra or observations are added. Code, aggregate scores, exact input hashes and separate-scratch repeat steps are included.

display.caption: Held-out event log loss for eight models, and differences for groups with at least 15 stars. Lower loss is better. All 25 groups enter total scores.
